objectives: Measure short-/e/ sound recognition separately from decoding.
Check short-/e/ spelling and sentence comprehension.
Identify developing fluency after accuracy is established.
Map errors to the correct remediation component.
concepts: A diagnostic should separate component skills.
Different error patterns require different interventions.

definitions.definition: An assessment used to identify strengths and specific learning gaps.
Accurate, appropriately paced and increasingly automatic reading.
Performing a learned skill with little conscious effort.

workedExamples: Strong recognition + weak decoding → review grapheme-to-phoneme blending.
Strong decoding + weak spelling → strengthen encoding.
Strong accuracy + slow reading → practise repeated accurate rereading.
Strong word reading + weak comprehension → strengthen meaning and evidence work.
commonMistakes: Treating all errors as decoding errors.
Using speed alone as the fluency measure.
Remediating everything instead of the diagnosed component.
Advancing without checking comprehension and spelling.
keyTakeaways: Map each error to its cause.
Use the result to plan targeted remediation.

application: Choose the correct remediation from diagnostic evidence.
higherOrderThinking: Differentiate an accuracy problem from an automaticity or comprehension problem.
mixedReview: Combine all short-/e/ skills in a diagnostic-style review.

formulaOrFactBank: Diagnostic result = component evidence, not a single speed score
mistakeBasedRevision: Slow + accurate → fluency practice; inaccurate → decoding repair; spelling errors → encoding repair.
weakTopicRevision: Reteach only the component indicated by the diagnostic evidence.

outcomes: Learner demonstrates short-/e/ recognition in controlled items.
Diagnostic distinguishes decoding, encoding, comprehension and fluency needs.
Teacher can identify the learner's highest-priority short-/e/ gap.
Results can drive targeted remediation and later reassessment.

questions.question: Which word is correctly decoded from b-e-d?
Which word has the same middle vowel as pen?
Which sequence shows accurate decoding?
options: Say sounds → blend → check the word

questions.question: Which word belongs to the -en family?
In “Ben has a red pen,” what does Ben have?
What happened first in a passage where Ben got a pen and then fed a hen?
A learner reads pen as pin. Which skill needs checking?
A learner spells bed as bid. Which skill needs checking?
Which action best supports developing fluency after accuracy is established?
options: Repeated accurate reading of controlled text

questions.question: Why separate decoding and fluency results in a diagnostic?
options: To identify whether the learner needs accuracy repair or automaticity practice

questions.question: If decoding is accurate but comprehension is weak, what should be targeted?
If spelling is weak but decoding is strong, what should be targeted?
What is the main purpose of this diagnostic?
options: Identify the learner's short-/e/ strengths and exact weak components for targeted remediation
